notes.title: The Spirit of the Samurai is Steam Deck Verified
notes.content:
Want to fight monstrous creatures inspired by Japanese mythology while on the go?

Now you can!

We’re excited to announce that The Spirit of the Samurai is now officially Steam Deck Verified.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43165389/b42274518a85063ae460105b79a9b725f9ea057e.png

But what does being Steam Deck Verified mean?

When a game is submitted for testing on the Steam Deck, it can be assigned one of three different badges depending on how it performs. The Unsupported badge means that the game does not run properly on the Steam Deck and the Playable badge means that the game can be played on the Steam Deck, but the player may need to make some manual adjustments to the game for it to function correctly.

The Verified badge is only awarded to games that operate well on the Steam Deck without the need for the player to make manual adjustments and don’t present any significant problems when it comes to installation, performance, controls, and display.

After a lot of hard work from the team, we’re so proud to have achieved Steam Deck Verified status for The Spirit of the Samurai!

The Spirit of the Samurai is a 2D stop-motion action adventure where you’ll get to play as three separate characters: the samurai Takeshi, his kitten Chisai, and the forest spirit Kodama. Traverse through beautifully realized 2.5D landscapes, fight against an army of horrifying monsters, and take on the demonic Shuten-dōji to save your village from total destruction. 

So why are we featuring in the Myths & Legends Sale?

The Myths & Legends Sale is designed to showcase games that were heavily inspired by the mythologies of different cultures, whether that be the yōkai of Japan or the jötunn of Norse legend. 

From the adorable forest spirits that populate Takeshi’s dreams to the horrifying spider-like creature Chisai must avoid to survive, every element of The Spirit of the Samurai has been inspired by the aesthetic, mythological characters, and legends of Japan.

Throughout the game, you’ll encounter the vicious hag Yama-uba, the towering Gashadokuro, and multiple other supernatural monstrosities known as yōkai torn straight from Japanese folklore.

notes.title: The Journey So Far
notes.content:
The path of the warrior always comes with obstacles and battles to be won, but the resulting peace is worth the fight.

We wanted to share with you our development journey so far and give you all a sneak peek at what’s on the horizon for The Spirit of the Samurai!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43165389/8547d8f65d70ed0d36e022be7766949d6120e221.png

Since our launch on December 12th 2024, our small team has continued to work steadily and very hard on The Spirit of the Samurai to improve the gameplay experience by listening to your feedback and suggestions, as well as adding new features and content. We’re extremely grateful to everyone who has taken the time to submit bug reports and give their feedback, which has helped us to make these updates and plan for the future of the game!

We’ve released two major updates so far, which came with quality of life improvements, balancing, improved combat controls, optimization of Steam Deck performance, a whole new cut-scene, and lots of bug fixes. If you want to know everything that was included in these updates, you can check out our patch notes for the first one here and the second one here.

So what does the road ahead look like for The Spirit of the Samurai?

We’re working on a third update at the moment, which will include a new enemy and brand new death cinematics! On top of that, we’ll also be adding more depth to the combo system, implementing more player feedback, and more bug fixes. 

After that, we plan to update the game regularly as soon as we have new improvements ready. All of these updates and all of the new content will be free for all players. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1507120/The_Spirit_of_the_Samurai/

Please do not hesitate to send us your suggestions and comments, since we’re listening to you and want your feedback for the future of the game!

Together we will make an even better game. Thank you for your help and trust!

You can submit your feedback in our Steam Forum or follow the links below to let us know on Discord and social media 🦊

notes.title: Patch #2: Steam Deck Performance Improvements and Even More Optimization!
notes.content:
We’re excited to let you all know that we’ve released our second patch for The Spirit of the Samurai!

Thank you once again for all of the players who have submitted their feedback and provided us with bug reports. We wouldn’t have been able to do this without your help!

Here are the major changes we’ve implemented in this patch:

 Regenerated all videos for the cut-scenes to Webm format, which is fully compatible with the Steam Deck and all other systems. This has eliminated all performance issues related to the cut-scenes on Steam Deck.
 Optimised performance on Steam Deck and lower spec PCs for increased stability and frame-rate (average 60 FPS).	
 Adjusted the visibility of the combo panel to better display on Steam Deck and smaller monitors.
 Improved the AI of the Undead enemies.
 Added new climbing points to the Tower level when you play as Chisai (the kitten).
 Combat balancing for Takeshi, particularly with the strength of his strikes.
 Improved controls during combat. Certain actions, such as the roll, can now be interrupted early so that players can attack if necessary. 
 Reduced VRAM usage (around 1.2GB) in the final fight and Kodama cave scene.
 Adjusted the hitboxes of Takeshi’s strikes so they’re more accurate. 
 Added a new cutscene featuring the Slave enemy type in the Dungeon level.
 General bug fixing.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1507120/The_Spirit_of_the_Samurai/

We’re still going to be gathering bug reports and feedback to form the basis for future patches, but we hope you enjoy the new and improved performance of The Spirit of the Samurai in this patch!

If you do encounter any bugs or would like to share any feedback with us, we’d love to hear from you in the Steam Forums, in our Discord, or on social media 🦊

notes.title: Patch #1: Combat Improvements, Performance Optimization, and Much More!
notes.content:
First of all, we’d like to say a huge thank you to all of the players who have taken the time to provide feedback and submit bug reports on The Spirit of the Samurai!

Your help has been invaluable when it has come to diagnosing the bugs that needed fixing and deciding on what quality of life changes to include in our first patch.

Thanks to you all, here are the major changes we’ve made in Build 1.0.06 based on player feedback:


 Responsiveness of Combat & Other Controls: We’ve improved combat and general movement controls to create a more fluid and consistent player experience. Parries are easier to execute effectively and the player character can now perform other actions while drinking potions or picking up items, so players can defend themselves more easily from incoming enemies. 
 Animation Speed: Character animations for the parry, item pick-up, and drinking health potions have been sped up.
 Level Navigation Improvements: The camera will now zoom out when players are navigating through the platforms in the Forest and Dungeon level, so that players have increased visibility when navigating the path ahead and jumping between platforms.
 Checkpoints & Shrines: We’ve added more checkpoints during the Basement, Forest, Cemetery, and Dungeon levels. We’ve also made it so that Shrines will function as checkpoints as well, meaning your game will now save after you’ve used the Shrine. We have also reduced the time it takes to offer items at the Shrine.
 Boss Balancing: We have balanced the bosses and made boss fights more challenging.
 Ranged Attacks: Archers and other ranged enemies will no longer attack you if they are off-screen.  
 Steam Deck Performance: We’ve improved performance of the game on the Steam Deck and have managed to achieve a consistent 90+ FPS in most areas. There are a few areas where players may still experience frame rate issues, but overall performance on the Steam Deck has improved considerably.
 4K Resolution: The bug causing black bars to appear around the screen in 4K resolution has been fixed, so you can enjoy The Spirit of the Samurai in the full glory of 4K!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1507120/The_Spirit_of_the_Samurai/

We’re still working on other quality of life changes, performance improvements, and bug fixes based on the feedback you’ve given us, but we hope that these changes will significantly enhance your experience of The Spirit of the Samurai!

If you do encounter any bugs or would like to share any feedback with us, we’d love to hear from you in the Steam Forums, in our Discord, or on social media 🦊

notes.title: Try Out Our Demo in Scream Fest!
notes.content:
The armies of Shuten-dōji are as ferocious as they are grotesque 👹

Will you have the courage to face off against these gruesome monsters inspired by Japanese folklore and rid Takeshi’s homeland of the horrors that plague it?

Find out if you’re a true samurai or just a scaredy-cat, because our new public demo is now available as part of Scream Fest!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43165389/769351634464b2cb6f5cce73859a04913b32f498.png

Scream Fest is the time to celebrate the spookiest season of the year with games that are sure to give you a delightful fright!

The Spirit of the Samurai draws deep inspiration from the horror tradition, with scenes and monsters inspired by the dark paintings of Zdzisław Beksiński, the monstrous artwork of H.R. Giger, and the uncanny stop-motion animation of Ray Harryhausen.

Set in a world inspired by Japanese mythology, you take on the role of three different characters throughout your journey: the samurai Takeshi, the kitten Chisai, and the forest spirit Kodama. Together, they must figure out a way to defeat the demonic Shuten-dōji before his armies take over.

In our demo, you’ll have the chance to play through a small portion of the story as the samurai Takeshi, try out our Combo Editor, and test your strength against some of Shuten-dōji’s warriors!

notes.title: Tengu: The Terror of the Skies
notes.content:
They may be bird-brained, but the Tengu is not an enemy you want to underestimate. What they lack in intelligence, they certainly make up for in martial skill.

Join us as we take a deep dive into the origins and inspiration behind this fowl beast!


https://store.steampowered.com/app/1507120/The_Spirit_of_the_Samurai/


Origin

It should come as no surprise that, like all of the other monsters and bosses from The Spirit of the Samurai, the tengu are legendary creatures originating from Japanese folklore. Within the indigenous religion of Shinto, they are categorised as a kami or godly spirit, but more generally they classed within popular culture as a supernatural being known as a yokai.

The first recorded mention of the word “tengu” in Japan can be traced back to a text known as the Nihon Shoki, which was written in 720 AD. According to this text, a Buddhist monk caught a glimpse of a huge shooting star, which he called a “heavenly dog” or tengu (天狗). This star immediately preceded a vicious military uprising, which led many to fear the tengu as harbingers of war. In these early interpretations, the tengu was most closely associated with the tiāngǒu, a legendary canine monster from Chinese mythology. As you can see, this is a far cry from the avian abomination we know today!

Over time, the tengu started to take on a more bird-like appearance, although the reasons behind this are unclear. Some scholasr speculate that the tengu’s current image was adapted based on that of a Hindu eagle deity known as a garuda, with the key difference being that garuda were friendly towards Buddhism, whereas tengu are traditional depicted as the troublesome enemies of Buddhism.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43165389/a1d86e9bb81c86ad82f7e44df8383adb3e4d0c4c.jpg

Regardless of how they underwent this feathery makeover, the tengu soon became cemented within Japanese folklore as loathsome and wretched creatures. Depictions from the 12th and 13th centuries described how they spent most of their time trying to mislead Buddhist monks, carry them off and drop in remote places, possess women to try to seduce them, rob temples, and tempt others to worship them by endowing them with unholy power. 

They were believed to be the ghosts of the arrogant, which is why they are now closely associated with vanity and pride. In fact, the phrase tengu ni naru (天狗になる) or “becoming a tengu” is still used in Japan today to describe an egotistical person!

From the 17th to the 19th century, however, repulsion towards the tengu had softened. Their reputation practically inverted as they began to be represented as pious followers of Buddhism, with some stories describing them protecting and blessing religious institutions rather than menacing them or setting them on fire.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43165389/0e0c8facf023148f497821f6531339bc963f27b4.jpg

They also came to be known as fearsome guardians of mountains and forests, with some regions of Japan still worshipping them to this day. There are now even festivals celebrating the tengu throughout Japan, including the annual Shimokitazawa Tengu Festival in Tokyo.

In short, this beaked beguiler is more than meets the eye!


Characteristics

Aside from its initial association with the canine creature tiāngǒu, the tengu have been traditionally depicted throughout Japanese history as anthropomorphic bird-like creatures. In particular, they carry many of the features of birds of prey, with long sharp beaks, piercing eyes, and talons on their hands or feet. There are, however, variations of tengu such as the Daitengu, who are depicted as predominantly human in appearance but with unnaturally long noses. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43165389/38cd959fa2ca430ff19442f2c85cf9b5dcafaa83.jpg

What unites all of these depictions of tengu is their reputation as exceptional martial artists. Stories abound with vivid descriptions of the tengu’s ferocious power and skill in battle, beginning with the legendary tale of the famous warrior Minamoto no Yoshitsune, who was supposedly trained in swordsmanship by the Tengu King Sōjōbō.

In other words, it’s going to take more than one stone to kill these birds!


Representation in The Spirit of the Samurai


With our feudal Japanese setting, we wanted to evoke older depictions of the tengu as grotesque harbingers of war. In-keeping with this theme, Tengu in The Spirit of the Samurai are vicious avian creatures with sharp beaks, blood-red eyes, dark wings, and taloned-claws clasped around their weapons.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43165389/d3156b1d00b967ade6fd6ce9996a51d2ff36bb70.png

We still wanted to retain the martial arts element of traditional tengu folklore, however, which is why the Tengu in our game fight using dual-wielded metal sickles based on Japanese kama. These sickles allow them to block attacks and inflict devastating blows on their opponents, so don’t pick a fight with the Tengu lightly!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43165389/5538d766f5f3ba25e8cf5be2623e543b9a7457cc.gif

What do you think of the Tengu?

Click the buttons below to let us know in our Discord server or on social media 🦊
